newsitem.title: USA: Celadon sees 20 pct revenue growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Celadon sees 20 pct revenue growth in 97.

text.p: Celadon Group Inc said on Wednesday it expected 20 percent revenue growth in fiscal 1997 and an operating ratio that trended to under 90 percent.
Chairman Steve Russell said that since management put into effect a turnaround strategy in June 1996, Celadon returned to profitability.
The company said an improving operating ratio was helping earnings.

"For the September 1996 quarter, our operating ratio improved to 93 percent," Russell said. "For the December quarter, we expect to report continued improvement... Importantly, each point of operating ratio equates to an annual impact in earnings per share of $0.15."

The truckload company said its turnaround strategy included focusing on its niche, strengthening operating management, cutting costs by $100,000 per week, improving driver retention, extending its Chrysler Corp contract and reducing its operating ratio to under 90 percent by mid-1997.
